 Order
Though the respondent is served with the notice, has chosen to remain absent.

The petitioner who is the husband has filed the present petition, assailing the order dated 01.09.2022 in Crl.Misc.No.226/2019 on the file of the Principal Judge, Family Court, Bagalkote,
whereby the petition filed by the wife seeking maintenance under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. came to allowed with cost and directed the petitioner-husband to pay monthly maintenance of Rs.10,000/-
p.m. to the respondent-wife from the date of filing of petition till her life time.
2.

Respondent-wife filed petition under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. seeking maintenance of Rs.25,000/-
from the petitioner-husband.
It is stated by the wife that the she is the legally wedded wife of the petitioner-respondent and marriage has been solemnized about 40 years prior to filing of the criminal miscellaneous petition.
It is stated that in the wedlock a daughter by name Mala has been born.
The husband has neglected to take care of the wife and child and as such she is constrained to file criminal miscellaneous seeking maintenance.
Several other allegations against the husband about having illicit relationship with other woman has been stated.
The suit for partition filed by the wife and her daughters being dismissed and the RA and second appeal filed by the petitioner has also been dismissed.
It is stated that the petitioner has married her daughter and requires financial support hence, filed petition.
3. Pursuant to the notice issued by the Trial Court, husband appeared and admitted their relationship and birth of their daughter.
However, the husband contended that the wife has left the matrimonial home without any reasonable cause, as such, is not entitled for maintenance as sought by the wife.
4. Wife examined herself as PW1 and got marked documents Ex.P1 to P4 and two witnesses as PWs.2 and 3.
On the other hand, husband examined himself as RW1, but, did not choose to produce any documents in support of his contention.

Concerned Family Court allowed the petition filed by the wife with cost of Rs.500/- and directed the husband to pay maintenance of Rs.10,000/- p.m. to the wife from the date of filing of petition till her life time.
5. Aggrieved by which, the present petition is filed by the husband.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the material on record.
7.
It is undisputed that petitioner and respondent are husband and wife and marriage having solemnized about 40 years back.

It appears due to uncordial relationship between the husband and Hanmant S/O Mukundappa More vs Smt Sulochana W/O Hanamant More on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125948779/

sentences.text: The Learned counsel for the petitioner-husband vehemently contends that petitioner is aged about 70 years and now has no source of income due to old age as such award of maintenance by the Family Court at Rs.10,000/- is excessive.
It is also stated that respondent-wife is sole responsible for having left the matrimonial home without reasonable cause and is not entitled for maintenance.

The material on record reveals that the land acquisition proceedings were initiated whereby the compensation was awarded of the SLAO and amount has been deposited and Ex.P1 is the order passed in LAC No.395/2012 wherein the husband was entitled for  share in the compensation awarded by the SLAO.
8. The husband is duty bound to maintain the wife and the plea that husband has no financial capacity is not available to the husband.
The intention of the legislature in enacting Sec.125 of Cr.P.C. is to see that the wife is not left in destitute for no fault of hers.

The Family Court by taking into consideration evidence of PW.1 to PW.3, the material on record that the husband has landed properties and has received the compensation amount in land acquisition proceedings and holding that the husband has failed to produce any material on record to show that wife has willfully neglected and staying away from the matrimonial home has held that the wife is entitled for maintenance and awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- p.m.
The manner in which the concerned Family Court has considered the pleadings and material on record and passed a considered order.
9. This Court is of the considered view that same does not call for any interference.

10. Accordingly, this Court pass the following:
ORDER a) The petition stands dismissed as devoid of merits.
b) The impugned order dated 01.09.2022 in Crl.Misc.No.226/2019 on the file of the Principal Judge, Family Court, Bagalkote stands confirmed.
